title: Geometric-Symmetry Logical Gate and Local-Probe Selectivity in the Three-Leg AKLT Ladder
abstract: Symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases provide a platform for encoding quantum information in protected boundary degrees of freedom. Here we study the three-leg Affleck-Kennedy-Lieb-Tasaki (AKLT) ladder as an exactly solvable SPT system with on-site symmetry $SO(3)\times \mathbb{Z}_2$. Using an exact matrix product state construction, we characterize the symmetry action on the edge encoding space and the accessibility of this space by local operators. We find that the continuous $SO(3)$ symmetry induces boundary rotations, while the leg-exchange symmetry generates a geometry-dependent logical permutation of edge qubits. Furthermore, by introducing a distinguishability measure motivated by the Knill--Laflamme condition, we derive a symmetry-resolved decay law for local accessibility. The decay is controlled by a selection rule raised from the Wigner--Eckart theorem, whereby a rank-$\ell$ local operator couples only to the $\mathcal L=\ell$ transfer-matrix sector, with a decay length determined by the corresponding correlation length. We further identify a finite-size channel that is independent of the probe operator position. These results establish a quantitative connection between SPT symmetry, lattice geometry, and the protection of boundary-encoded quantum information.
summary: The authors investigate how symmetry protects quantum information encoded on the boundaries of a three-leg AKLT ladder. They derive a quantitative decay law showing that local probe operators can only access specific symmetry sectors, leading to an observable hierarchy in correlation lengths. This establishes a rigorous link between lattice geometry, underlying symmetries, and the robustness of topological quantum memory.
main_problem: The study aims to establish a quantitative connection between Symmetry-Protected Topological (SPT) symmetry, lattice geometry, and the protection of boundary-encoded quantum information.
main_result: The paper shows that local operator accessibility decay is governed by selection rules derived from symmetries, leading to an observable hierarchy of correlation lengths in the three-leg AKLT ladder.
method: The analysis uses exact Matrix Product State (MPS) constructions and channel decomposition techniques motivated by the Knill--Laflamme condition to quantify information leakage.
model_or_system: The system studied is the three-leg Affleck-Kennedy-Lieb-Tasaki (AKLT) ladder, an exactly solvable SPT model with on-site symmetry SO(3) x Z2. It is analyzed using MPS representations derived from a frustration-free parent Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Logical gates ($	ext{SO}(3)$ rotations and permutation), local operator accessibility decay law $\delta_{	ext{edge}}(	ext{dist}) \propto e^{-	ext{dist}/\xi(L=\ell)}$, and the hierarchy of correlation lengths $\xi(L=1) > \xi(L=2) > \xi(L=3)$.
important_parameters: The symmetry labels (SO(3) tensor rank and $P_{tb}$ parity), the lattice geometry (three-leg ladder vs. single chain), and the correlation lengths $\xi(L)$ are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on projecting the system onto relevant sectors ($L$-sectors) and assuming that the decay law can be accurately modeled by retaining leading eigenvalues in the channel decomposition.

paper_structure: The paper first characterizes the symmetries and logical gates using MPS. It then introduces a distinguishability measure based on channel decomposition of the transfer matrix. Finally, it derives the symmetry-resolved decay law for local accessibility, showing how different $L$-sectors contribute distinct correlation lengths.
why_interesting: This work provides quantitative metrics (decay laws, selection rules) linking fundamental symmetries to concrete measures of quantum information protection in lattice models, which is highly relevant for understanding robust quantum memories and computation architectures.
